headline: Thanksgiving and Friday are sunny, dry and very warm with morning Santa Ana gusts, Friday peaking 12 to 15 degrees above normal, while a big swell and exceptionally high tides flood parts of the coast this morning; models agree strongly on a moderate to strong storm Tuesday–Wednesday with 1 to 3 inches of rain for the coasts and valleys.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Thanksgiving is sunny, dry and very warm around Glendale and across Southern California, with locally gusty Santa Ana (northeast) winds this morning. Highs reach the upper 70s to mid 80s across the coasts and valleys south of Point Conception and the mid 70s to lower 80s farther north, about 10 to 15 degrees above normal, under mostly clear skies with maybe some high clouds. Gusts should reach low-end advisory levels in the Santa Lucia Mountains, Santa Susana Mountains and western San Gabriel Mountains, with Wind Advisories until 2 PM today for some areas and until 9 AM Friday for others, while other wind-prone spots stay just below advisory levels. Light turbulence and wind shear are possible near Burbank, Van Nuys and Camarillo this morning.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Gusty Santa Ana winds return Friday morning, though a little weaker overall, and Friday is the warmest day, 1 to 3 degrees warmer than Thanksgiving with highs 12 to 15 degrees above normal. On Saturday the offshore winds are noticeably weaker and an ocean breeze may return in the afternoon, cooling things 4 to 8 degrees, though highs stay above normal. It stays dry through Saturday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Sunday brings increasing clouds and 3 to 6 degrees of cooling, with rain chances on the Central Coast in the afternoon and rain likely there Sunday evening, while LA stays dry until a 20 to 30 percent chance of light rain develops south of Point Conception Sunday night. The latest update calls the Sunday afternoon to Monday morning rain very light, with some areas possibly getting little to none; the overnight discussion had Monday cloudy with a 30 to 40 percent chance of rain, up to a quarter to a third of an inch on coast-facing slopes and the Central Coast, and highs near normal. Then all forecast models agree remarkably well on a moderate to strong cold storm dropping in from the north Tuesday or Tuesday night, with the heaviest rain Tuesday tapering off Wednesday: 1 to 3 inches for the coasts and valleys, 3 to 5 inches on coast-facing slopes and half an inch to 1.5 inches in the far interior, plus a chance of thunderstorms if the storm center passes overhead. Snow should only stick above about 7,500 feet, and highs will mostly be in the 60s Tuesday and Wednesday.

coast: A large, long-period west swell combines with exceptionally high tides to bring large surf and moderate to significant coastal flooding this morning, worst at the morning high tide and in low-lying spots with no protection from the ocean; much above normal tides continue into Friday morning. The biggest surf and worst flooding are on the Central Coast from Point Conception northward, the Ventura County coast and far eastern parts of the southern Santa Barbara County coast, where Coastal Flood Warnings run until noon today and High Surf Warnings until noon, followed by High Surf Advisories lasting until noon or 9 PM Saturday depending on the stretch of coast; other beaches see somewhat lesser but still concerning impacts under Coastal Flood Advisories until noon and High Surf Advisories until noon or 9 PM today. Expect strong rip currents nearly everywhere, strong along-shore currents, sneaker waves, heavy shore break, coastal erosion and a higher risk of damage to coastal structures, making swimming dangerous. On the water, large breaking waves near the coast and harbor entrances can capsize small boats today; Small Craft Advisories run until 3 PM today, 3 AM Friday or 3 AM Saturday depending on the area, with advisory-strength offshore winds near shore from Point Mugu to Santa Monica this afternoon and rough seas on the outer waters and north of Point Sal through Friday night. Conditions are mostly calmer Saturday through Monday, then winds increase to advisory levels or higher Monday night ahead of the strong midweek storm.
watch_for: Coastal flooding and dangerous surf at this morning's high tide, worst on the Central Coast and Ventura County coast
Gusty Santa Ana winds in the Santa Susana, western San Gabriel and Santa Lucia Mountains this morning and again Friday morning
The Tuesday–Wednesday storm: 1 to 3 inches of rain for the coasts and valleys and 3 to 5 inches on the slopes, with timing that could shift by about 12 hours
confidence: Forecasters see very little doubt in the warm, dry stretch through Saturday, call the agreement among models on a moderate to strong Tuesday–Wednesday storm remarkable though its timing could shift by about 12 hours, and have moderate to high confidence in the marine forecast.
